newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Sievert- No need to change German rates.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Sievert- No need to change German rates.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert said on Thursday that he saw no need to change German interest rates and that inflation prospects for the current year were favourable.
Sievert said in the text of a speech that the Bundesbank's steady hand policy since last summer was reasonable.

"Nothing has changed in this regard as far as we are concerned. There is no current leeway for further rate cuts. On the other hand, there is also no reason to consider higher rates in the near future," Sievert said.

Sievert, also president of the state central bank for Saxony and Thuringia, said the outlook for inflation this year appeared favourable due to strong competition and a weak economic recovery. Nor was there any inflation danger from the costs side, he said.
Turning to developments in M3 money supply this year, Sievert noted that growth in money supply so far was stronger than had been expected.
Money supply rose moderately in February and March, he said, noting that the April growth figure was 6.7 percent -- close to the Bundesbank's target range of 3.5 to 6.5 percent.
However, he said: "The developments in the first months still say very little about whether the M3 target growth rate can be achieved this year."
That was because M3 had been influenced by the customary volatility of the early months and thus was not as significant as later developments, he said.
